claims.text: The material family of interest is face-centered cubic Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys.
The targeted property for improvement is saturation magnetization (Ms).
The primary scientific challenge is an inability to decouple the orbital magnetic moment from the spin magnetic moment.
Strong spin-orbit coupling and crystal-field quenching cause the stated difficulty in separating orbital and spin moments.
The inability to decouple orbital and spin moments prevents optimization of the total magnetic moment for soft-magnetic applications.
Equiatomic or near-equiatomic fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys exhibit high saturation magnetization.
These alloys have low magnetic anisotropy and a quenched orbital moment.
A 1-5 at% addition of Ru, Rh, or Os can be incorporated into the Fe-Co-Ni fcc lattice without phase separation or alteration of the fcc structure.
The heavy dopant induces local symmetry breaking and modifies the d-band electronic structure near the Fermi level.
Dopant-induced electronic-structure changes lift d-orbital degeneracy and reduce crystal-field quenching of the orbital moment.
The heavy dopant increases the effective spin-orbit coupling constant and partially unquenches the orbital magnetic moment.
Partial orbital-moment unquenching increases the total magnetic moment per atom.
Heavy-element doping may enhance the magnetic anisotropy energy.
The proposed mechanism can yield higher permeability and lower coercivity if magnetic anisotropy remains sufficiently low.
Heavy-dopant addition will produce a measurable increase in the orbital-to-spin moment ratio detectable by XMCD.
The increased orbital-to-spin moment ratio will lead to either increased saturation magnetization or significantly enhanced magnetic anisotropy without loss of fcc stability.
In standard fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys, the cubic crystal field nearly fully quenches the orbital moment, so magnetism is dominated solely by spin.
Exceeding the dopant solubility limit may form secondary sigma or B2 phases, while sufficiently large lattice-parameter changes may induce a magnetic or structural phase transition.

contradictions.description: Low magnetic anisotropy is described as a limitation in the initial state, but the mechanism says anisotropy must remain low to preserve soft-magnetic behavior, while the predicted outcome treats a significant anisotropy enhancement as a possible improvement.

Strong spin-orbit coupling is initially presented as part of the cause of the orbital/spin decoupling problem, whereas increasing spin-orbit coupling is subsequently proposed as the remedy; the distinction between moment separation and orbital-moment unquenching is not resolved.
